issues.title: Verify evals on Papers with Code
issues.body:
Hi,

Niels here from the open-source team at Hugging Face. Congratulations on your work!

I've made the [paper](https://paperswithcode.co/paper/2601.22032) and [4 verified paper-native evaluations](https://paperswithcode.co/paper/2601.22032#results) available on Papers with Code.

The paper is part of the [Autonomous Driving](https://paperswithcode.co/tasks/autonomous-driving) task page.

The Drive-JEPA (ViT/L) result currently ranks first on [NAVSIM v1](https://paperswithcode.co/benchmark/navsim-v1?task=autonomous-driving&eval=17730).

The Drive-JEPA ViT/L result currently ranks first on [NAVSIM v2 navtest](https://paperswithcode.co/benchmark/navsim-v2-navtest?task=autonomous-driving&eval=17756).

The Drive-JEPA results currently rank fourth on [two metrics on Bench2Drive v0.0.3](https://paperswithcode.co/benchmark/bench2drive-v0-0-3?task=autonomous-driving&eval=17731).

Would it be possible to verify these results and let me know if any score, model name, benchmark protocol, or openness metadata should be corrected? The imported rows are tied to the paper or its official release artifacts; comparison-table baselines were not added.

You can also edit the task, methods, project page, and GitHub URL directly from the paper page using your Hugging Face account.

If you'd like to showcase the results in your repository README, you can copy these live leaderboard badges (or use the “Copy PwC badge” button in the Results section):

[![Papers with Code: SOTA on NAVSIM v1](https://paperswithcode.co/api/v1/papers/2601.22032/leaderboard-badge.svg?eval=17730&live=1)](https://paperswithcode.co/benchmark/navsim-v1?task=autonomous-driving&eval=17730)

[![Papers with Code: SOTA on NAVSIM v2 navtest](https://paperswithcode.co/api/v1/papers/2601.22032/leaderboard-badge.svg?eval=17756&live=1)](https://paperswithcode.co/benchmark/navsim-v2-navtest?task=autonomous-driving&eval=17756)

Kind regards,

Niels

issues.title: Question about training time for Drive-JEPA planner training
issues.body:
Hi authors,

Thanks for releasing the code and checkpoints. I am trying to reproduce the Drive-JEPA planner training on NAVSIM v1.

I noticed that the paper mentions the planner training setup:
- 20 epochs
- 2 NVIDIA A30 GPUs
- batch size 64

However, I could not find the approximate training time in the paper or repository.

Could you please provide:
1. The approximate training time for the planner training stage (20 epochs) on 2×A30 GPUs?
2. Whether this time includes the dataset/cache preprocessing stage or only the optimization stage?
3. Approximately how long does generating the training cache take?

This information would be very helpful for reproduction.

Thanks a lot!

issues.title: Awesome Driving World Models
issues.body:
Dear authors,

We are from WorldBench and are maintaining relevant GitHub repositories, [awesome-3d-4d-world-models](https://github.com/worldbench/awesome-3d-4d-world-models) and [awesome-vla-for-ad](https://github.com/worldbench/awesome-vla-for-ad), which collect recent and representative works related to 3D and 4D world modeling and autonomous driving, just like Drive-JEPA. 

These two repositories are affiliated with our survey papers, “[3D and 4D World Modeling: A Survey](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.07996)” and “[Vision-Language-Action Models for Autonomous Driving: Past, Present, and Future](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.16760)”. We plan to incorporate newly released papers into the next version of the surveys.

If you are open to it, we would be glad to include your preprint in these repositories. Please feel free to let me know, or you may also add it directly via a pull request.

Thank you for your time, and I appreciate your contribution to this research direction.

Best regards,
Lingdong, on behalf of the [WorldBench](https://github.com/worldbench) team

issues.title: Release Drive-JEPA artifacts (models, dataset) on Hugging Face
issues.body:
Hello,

Niels here from the open-source team at Hugging Face. I discovered your work through Hugging Face's daily papers as yours got featured: https://huggingface.co/papers/2601.22032.
The paper page lets people discuss about your paper and lets them find artifacts about it (your models, datasets or demo for instance), you can also claim
the paper as yours which will show up on your public profile at HF, add Github and project page URLs.

I noticed in your GitHub README that you are planning to release the code and checkpoints for Drive-JEPA soon. It'd be great to make the checkpoints and the curated driving video dataset available on the 🤗 hub to improve their discoverability and visibility.
We can add tags so that people find them when filtering https://huggingface.co/models and https://huggingface.co/datasets.

## Uploading models

See here for a guide: https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/models-uploading.

In this case, we could leverage the [PyTorchModelHubMixin](https://huggingface.co/docs/huggingface_hub/package_reference/mixins#huggingface_hub.PyTorchModelHubMixin) class which adds `from_pretrained` and `push_to_hub` to any custom `nn.Module`. Alternatively, one can leverages the [hf_hub_download](https://huggingface.co/docs/huggingface_hub/en/guides/download#download-a-single-file) one-liner to download a checkpoint from the hub.

We encourage researchers to push each model checkpoint to a separate model repository, so that things like download stats also work. We can then also link the checkpoints to the paper page.

## Uploading dataset

Would be awesome to make the curated driving dataset available on 🤗 , so that people can do:

```python
from datasets import load_dataset

dataset = load_dataset("your-hf-org-or-username/your-dataset")
```
See here for a guide: https://huggingface.co/docs/datasets/loading.

Besides that, there's the [dataset viewer](https://huggingface.co/docs/hub/en/datasets-viewer) which allows people to quickly explore the first few rows of the data in the browser.

Let me know if you're interested/need any help regarding this!

Cheers,

Niels
ML Engineer @ HF 🤗
